build.description: Build project: generate code, transpile library and/or compile bundled output.

metafile.description: Write bun's markdown module-graph report (--metafile-md, Bun 1.4) next to the transpiled output, one per build graph

timeout-budget.description: Wall-clock timeout for the test subprocess in milliseconds

rerun-each.description: Re-run each test file N times

only.description: Only run tests marked with test.only()

coverage.description: Per-project coverage policy. Set false to opt a project out of coverage entirely (authoritative — the validation cadence never overrides it).

enforce-coverage.description: Enforce each project's coverage-threshold. On by default so a coverage drop fails the run that caused it. Pass --no-enforce-coverage to keep measuring and reporting coverage without failing on the threshold; to skip instrumentation entirely use --coverage=false, which this never overrides.

coverage-threshold.description: Minimum required line coverage percentage (0 disables the gate). Fails the test job when coverage is below it. Enforced by default; --no-enforce-coverage zeroes it for the run while still reporting coverage. Configurable per workspace, language, or project.

parallel.description: Opt-in bun test worker processes (Bun 1.4): true for --parallel, a number for --parallel=N. Off by default — the putnami DAG already runs projects in parallel.

test-verbose.description: Show the complete test transcript at info level; changes visibility only, never the Bun invocation or verdict

kill-port.description: Kill process using port before starting

run.description: Run a workload once for the host and forward its exit code.

entrypoint.description: Entry point to run (defaults to ./run export, then main)

port.description: Port (set via the PORT environment variable)

args.description: Additional arguments to pass to the program

skip-guard.description: Refuse a focused test (`.only(`) and a test skip without a guard, or with a guard that names flakiness or CI. A reviewed exception is written `// putnami:allow-skip <reason>` and reported as a warning.

docs-links.description: Check every relative link and anchor in the project's README.md files and doc/ trees; a broken one fails lint.

docker-registry.description: Publish target compatibility flag; local packaging ignores it

workspace-builder-image.description: Workspace builder image for CI multi-stage builds

docker-base-image.description: Override the digest-pinned base image (must include @sha256:... for reproducible digests)

docker-base-project.description: Use the typed local OCI candidate of this graph dependency as the image base

docker-load.description: Also load the assembled image into the local docker daemon

dry-run.description: Show what would be packaged without creating artifacts

publish.description: Publish pre-built packages to registries (npm and Docker). Auto-runs package first; that pipeline owns every required build step while its image-project branch stays compiler-free. @putnami/cloud, when installed, provides advanced publishing; otherwise native registry credentials are used.

dry-run.description: Show what would be published without uploading

config-extract.description: Extract config schema from the workload to schema/config.json (committed; options.generate.schema=false falls back to .gen/config-schema.json)

workspace-fetch.description: Download the packages the committed bun.lock names into bun's cache, running none of their code.

force.description: Force reinstall even if bun.lock is up to date

workspace-sync.description: Synchronize TypeScript-owned workspace state (package workspaces, package names).

cache-clean.description: Purge the TypeScript incremental scratch this extension owns. Bun's shared package cache is deliberately left alone: one worktree's cold rebuild must not cost every checkout on the machine its downloads.

cache-gc.description: Bound the TypeScript incremental scratch and the Bun package cache to their budgets.

deps-upgrade.description: Upgrade @putnami/* framework dependencies to latest versions.

putnami.typescript_docs.description: Return the AI.md bytes from the exact npm package resolved for one TypeScript project. Resolution walks that project's node_modules ancestry in Node order, verifies the installed package name and version, and never invokes Bun, installs dependencies, consults a registry, or substitutes extension-carried docs. Omit project only when the reference identifies exactly one declaring TypeScript project.

reference.description: Exact npm package name, for example @putnami/web

project.description: Optional Putnami project name, npm package name, or workspace-relative project directory

cache-clean-exec.description: Remove the ts-types incremental scratch this extension writes under the worktree cache root. Bun's shared package cache is deliberately left alone (GC bounds it; clean never wipes it). Declares no outputs and the toolchain-cache effect: it mutates machine-global state no cache hit could reproduce.

cache-gc-exec.description: Evict ts-types scratch untouched within its grace window and bound Bun's package cache to its byte budget. Declares no outputs and the toolchain-cache effect.

build-generate.description: Generate code into the project's .gen subtree (and, when the project generates one, the configured TypeScript client directory). Ownership decision: build-generate is the SINGLE producer of <project>/.gen — every other task that writes inside it (config-extract-exec's .gen/config-schema.json fallback) writes into generate-owned territory rather than claiming a slice of it. Its v3 `declares` block is deliberately still absent: six commands (build, test, serve, run, package, config-extract) schedule this one task, and the plan-time owner check counts each of those plan nodes as a separate owner of <project>/.gen, so declaring it today makes every multi-command TypeScript plan (`putnami lint,test,build`) unplannable. The declaration lands with the CLI change that treats repeated scheduling of ONE task for ONE project as one owner; until then this task keeps v2 inferred capture via its gen/clients write resources.

data.description: Generated code metadata and exports map

clientOutput.description: Project-relative directory of the generated TypeScript client, reported only when the client generator emitted one. This is the pathFrom anchor for the clients half of the ownership decision above: the directory is chosen by the project's clientgen config, so it is declarable only through this port. The consumer reads it under this exact name.

gen.description: Generated sources: the whole project-rooted .gen subtree, owned exclusively by this task (config-extract's schema fallback inside .gen is this task's output, not a second owner).

client.description: Generated TypeScript client at the config-chosen directory the clientOutput port reports; absent when the project generates no client. The client is committed, and this task is the FIRST writer of that directory in a session, so the engine compares what it writes (or a cache hit restores) with the bytes present before and fails the task on a difference — the worktree then holds the regenerated client to commit (protocols/extension ADR 0004). The project document a workspace commits inside the directory, and the dependency install the workspace materializes there when the client is a package of its own, are preserved: never captured, restored over, or judged (protocols/extension ADR 0005). The client project's own .gen directory, which the engine and that project's tasks write, is preserved the same way.

capabilities.description: The project's capability manifest, promoted out of .gen into the tracked tree when the project sets options.generate.capabilities. The framework producer is its sole author; this task only copies what it wrote, the same split the Go extension keeps between describe and promotion. Absent for every project that does not opt in.

openapi.description: The project's committed OpenAPI contract, written by the application's openapi() document at slot 0 during this task's pre-build hook — the one document clientGenerator(), workspace client discovery and compose read. It is committed, and this task is its first writer in a session, so the engine compares what it writes (or a cache hit restores) with the bytes present before and fails the task with generated-output-drift on a difference — the worktree then holds the regenerated contract to commit (protocols/extension ADR 0004). Absent for a project without openapi(), or whose document sets output to false or to another path.

lib.description: Transpiled JavaScript library. Sole owner of <command-output>/lib; sibling steps own types/ and compile/. Empty when the project resolves no entrypoint.

types.description: Emitted .d.ts declarations. Sole owner of <command-output>/types. Empty when tsc emits nothing.

build-compile.description: Compile the project's entrypoint into standalone bun executables. The target set is scoped by PACKAGE CHANNEL: under `package --docker` the compile is bound to the image's `platform` and produces that one bun target, because an image carries one executable and the other three were compiled and discarded; `--compile-target` still names one target and wins; every other invocation keeps the full four-target distribution matrix. Both deciding inputs (`docker`, `platform`) are declared `from: "params"`, so the resolved set is a plan-time cache-key participant and a four-target entry can never answer a one-target request. The docker intent is read as a parameter rather than from the project's `publish` declaration because a parameter is what the key can see and what a batched invocation shares across its members; a project that declares the channel without `options.package.docker` still packages an image and simply keeps the full set — extra targets, never a missing one.

compile.description: Compiled bundle/executable. Sole owner of <command-output>/compile. Empty when the project resolves no compile entrypoint.

build-infra.description: Aggregate the workload's deployability requirements into <project>/.gen/requirements.json: every project in the workload's dependency closure contributes its committed infra/requirements.json, the workload's infra/overrides.json suppresses what it does not want, and its infra/runtime.json (or the framework defaults sidecar) supplies the runtime block. Extension-owned since an earlier migration — the CLI used to gate and write this artifact itself, and to decide, by matching project tags and extension names, that a TypeScript workload must run without HTTP/2. That compatibility statement now lives HERE, where Bun's h2c support is a fact this extension owns. Libraries are skipped: they are consumed, never deployed. Ownership decision: it declares NO outputs, for the same reason as config-extract-exec's schema fallback — everything it writes lands under <project>/.gen, which build-generate owns whole as its single producer. Never cached: its inputs are OTHER projects' committed manifests, which no per-project cache key can cover, and it is a few small file reads.

data.description: Aggregation outcome (emitted, cleared, skipped), the manifest path, and the number of contributing projects
Combined read-only format + lint result with diagnostics

lint-docs.description: Documentation link check: every relative link and anchor in the project's README.md files and doc/ trees must resolve, with the case of the file on disk. The task body is the SDK's docslinks.Job, shared with every language extension. UNCACHEABLE on purpose: a link may name any file of the workspace, so no file-pattern key covers the read set, and a key that missed a deleted target would serve a green verdict for a broken link.

test-env-up.description: Provision the database test environment this project's tests run against, and write the resolved binding into the invocation-scoped sensitive artifact `test-run` reads. Extension-owned since an earlier migration — the CLI used to discover the datasources, run the container and inject the binding through a private env seam it then had to hide from its own cache key. Policy is unchanged: an externally supplied DATABASE_TEST_BINDINGS always wins, `--infra` (auto|require|skip) steers the mode with the CI default `require`, `--infra-down` tears every workspace-labeled container down and provisions nothing, and only a local `auto` run with docker on PATH ever touches the docker CLI. NEVER FAILS: an environment that could not be provisioned is reported by the test run itself, which skips its live cases when no binding is present.

data.description: Test-environment outcome (provisioned, external, no-databases, not-provisioned, torn-down), the resolved mode, the datasource count and the server configuration digest. Credential-free by construction.

bindings.description: The resolved database test binding (credentials included). Invocation-scoped and sensitive: it lives at mode 0600 in the invocation's private tree, is never captured or restored, and dies with the invocation. Absent whenever this run provisioned nothing.

lease.description: Non-secret record of the provisioned server (invocation id, label, configuration digest, container name, retention intent) the finalizer reclaims by. Has no free-form member, so it can never carry a credential onto a label or filter.

test-env-down.description: Finalize the database test environment: read the non-secret lease and do what it says. The ordinary run RETAINS its server — a still-running container whose configuration digest matches is interchangeable across invocations, and the next `test-env-up` reaps every digest-mismatched container before it reuses or starts one — while an `--infra-down` lease sweeps. Runs with `runOn: finally`, so the orchestrator runs it exactly once whenever `test-env` STARTED, consumer failure and cancellation included.

data.description: Test execution result with pass/fail counts

coverage.description: Merged lcov report; absent unless coverage is instrumented (--enforce-coverage). The per-worker .lcov.info.*.tmp shards are deleted before the task returns and are never an output.

junit.description: JUnit report; absent when the project has no test files.

featureVerification.description: The reserved run-scoped feature verification report: the merged observations of every test bound to a declared check through @putnami/runtime/spectest. Absent when no test in the project bound one. Written per member under batching, so per-project attribution and cache restore hold for both the singleton and the batched run — a cache hit that lost this report would silently disarm the spec gate.

npm.description: Assembled npm package directory and the npm channel record (npm/channel.json). Sole owner of <command-output>/npm; it reads (never writes) the lib/ and types/ trees its sibling build steps own. Absent when the project has no publishable build output. Recording the channel INSIDE this directory is what keeps the task under ordinary declared capture: the record is restored with the package it describes, and the channel index publish reads is derived over every packager's record (pkgmeta.ReadChannelIndex) instead of kept as a shared file.

package-docker.description: Assemble a local OCI image candidate from compiled output or a first-class image project's spec. It never resolves an output registry or emits publication evidence; the mutually exclusive paths share this single owner of <command-output>/docker. Every task under `package` writes only inside its declaration and is captured the ordinary way.

docker.description: Local OCI candidate layout, manifest (candidate digest, platform, content identity, and relative artifact location only) and the docker channel record (docker/channel.json). Sole owner of <command-output>/docker; it reads the compile/ tree its sibling step owns and never contains a published immutable reference. Absent on a dry run. Like package-npm, it records its channel inside the directory it owns — see the note on package-npm's declared output.

published-image.description: Publish-owned verified remote image record. Present only after registry digest verification: this task writes it when it pushes the image, and the engine writes it when this task packs the image into a publication outbox. Package never writes or rewrites it.

schema.description: Path to the emitted schema/config.json (or .gen/config-schema.json fallback)

Committed config manifest. Absent when the workload registers no config blocks, or when options.generate.schema=false routes the manifest to the .gen/config-schema.json fallback — that fallback lives inside the .gen subtree build-generate owns, so it is captured there and is deliberately not claimed here.

jsonSchema.description: JSON Schema companion of schema/config.json, emitted and absent under exactly the same conditions.

data.description: Project version metadata (name, version, sha, branch, isDirty, buildTime)
